source: data/cache/xpts.json (GW1 priors: form, xgi_per90, fdr) + data/cache/league.json (GW1 ownership empty -> ownership inferred from price tier / xpts rank)

transfers.note: GW1 initial squad build — no transfers exist. Free transfer banked for GW2 (target: react to opening-weekend minutes/lineup data before committing).

chip_rationale: APEX chip-timing gates all unmet at GW1: no DGW (TC/BB), no BGW (FH), and zero rotation flags from a fresh squad (WC). Saving all four chips is strictly higher EV than a GW1 punt.

differentials.case: Model's 8th-ranked asset overall and the single best xPts-per-million pick in the dataset outside of Raya. FDR 2 fixture, attacking full-back profile at a £5.0m entry price that almost nobody starts GW1 on.

Cheap route into the MCI attack at 6.5. Outscores every mid priced 6.0-7.5 in the model (beats Szoboszlai 4.92, Gravenberch 4.17, Foden 3.10, Cherki 3.49) while the crowd pays 7.5-9.5 for Palmer (2.86) and Saka (4.97).
Enabler forward. Best xPts of any sub-£6.5m striker and beats Gyökeres (3.14 @ 7.5) and João Pedro (3.60 @ 7.5) on value, freeing 1.5m that funds Gabriel in defence.

captain_rationale: APEX captaincy protocol = nailed premium, never a GK. No cum_pts table exists at GW1, so the tiebreak falls to highest captain_xpts among owned players: Haaland 16.26. B.Fernandes projects higher (18.26) but at £12.0m alongside Haaland's £15.5m the 27.5m premium spend collapses the rest of the squad to sub-5.0m filler — the model's own numbers show that trade costs ~2.2 net XI xPts. Haaland is also the top10k safe haven: captaining him caps downside vs the field.
strategy_notes: top10k pattern: 3-4-3, safe-haven core (Haaland + Raya + Gabriel + Rice + Gibbs-White = 5 of the model's top 6 assets) plus 3 calculated sub-radar picks.
The GW1 model is defence-skewed: Raya 8.50, Gabriel 8.34, Guéhi 7.00, N.Williams 6.66 all outrank every forward except Haaland. I bought that edge rather than chasing forwards.

Deliberately skipped B.Fernandes (9.13, £12.0m). Pairing him with Haaland burns 27.5m on two players and forces four sub-5.5m starters; the model says that build lands ~69.7 XI xPts vs 71.9 for this one.
Also faded the price traps the crowd will own: Palmer 2.86 @ 9.5, Isak 0.50 @ 9.0, Ekitiké 0.00 @ 7.5, Šeško 0.67 @ 7.0, Wirtz 2.81 @ 7.5. Being underweight there is where the rank comes from.

Known cost of the mandated 3-4-3: Shaw (5.73) and Hume (5.28) sit on the bench while Calvert-Lewin (3.23) starts. A 4-4-2 or 3-5-2 would score ~2.5 higher on paper, but 3-4-3 keeps three attacking returns live and is the shape the top10k playbook specifies.
Bench order puts Yarmoliuk first so an early forward/mid non-start is covered before the defensive slots are disturbed.
